pr_title: Don't write 0 to next modbus register
pr_body:
Don't write a 0 to the register+1 when updating the target temperature. Fixes #48027

<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Using `[value,0]` writes a 0 to a modbus register of value `register`+1 after writing the `value` to `register`.
This causes all sorts of unwanted side effects as described in #48027 
This is fixed by using `value` instead.

issue_context.title: ModBus Climate sets temperature to 0 after calling set_temperature
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I'm using the modbus interface to read and control my Mitsubishi EcoDan EHST20D Heat Pump. (config below) 
When updating the target temperature, the temperature on the thermostat briefly changes to the correct amount, and then changes to 0.0 °C.


### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.3.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

ModBus Climate

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/climate.modbus/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Mitsubishi EcoDan Heat Pump
climates:
 - name: EHST20D
   slave: 4
   target_temp_register: 54
   current_temp_register: 94
   data_type: int
   data_count: 1
   precision: 1
   scale: 0.01
   max_temp: 25
   min_temp: 10
   temp_step: 0.5
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
# Put your logs below this line

```


I suspect the issue to be in this line of code:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/009e44ed9b7e2c2fad662cfea23e6490d0e24a42/homeassistant/components/modbus/climate.py#L277

This seems to cause the modbus integration to write the correct temperature value to the register, followed by a 0. This in turn sets the heat pump target temperature to 0 °C
comments:
Hey there @adamchengtkc, @janiversen, @vzahradnik, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L288) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I tested setting the temperature via a service call. This sets the temperature correctly: (20°C)
```yaml
service: modbus.write_register
data:
  hub: pi01
  unit: 4
  address: 54
  value: 2000
```
The ModBus Climate integration is doing something equal to this, which sets the temperature to 0°C:
```yaml
service: modbus.write_register
data:
  hub: pi01
  unit: 4
  address: 54
  value: [2000, 0]
```

I have a similar issue.
Home Assistant Operating System on raspberry with core-2021.3.0
I have 6 ModBus Climate, with ModBus TCP.
When I update the target temperature of one climate, the target temperature of another random climate change to zero, not always the same.
It doesn't always happen.
I tried to change delay and timeout in modbus config but nothing has changed.
Any ideas?

My configuration:
```
modbus:
  name: hub1
  type: tcp
  host: 192.168.123.49
  port: 502
  delay: 5
  
  climates:
      - name: Bagno Notte
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 25
        current_temp_register: 33
      - name: Camera Matrimoniale
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 29
        current_temp_register: 34
      - name: Cameretta
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 30
        current_temp_register: 35
      - name: Bagno Giorno
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 28
        current_temp_register: 36
      - name: Camera Grande
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 31
        current_temp_register: 37
      - name: Zona Giorno
        slave: 255
        data_type: uint
        data_count: 1
        scale: 0.1
        offset: 0
        precision: 1
        max_temp: 30
        min_temp: 10
        temp_step: 0.1
        target_temp_register: 32
        current_temp_register: 38

```

I think I see what's happening here, the 0 is being written to `target_temp_register + 1`.
My heatpump responds has two registers for each thermostat, one signed and one unsigned. The integration will write the `target_temp` to `target_temp_register` and then a 0 to `target_temp_register + 1`. 
In my case this means my thermostat will be overwritten to 0, since the next register is the unsigned one. 
In your case it is overwriting the next register, so for ex when setting: "Camera Grande" (register 32)  the "Zone Giorno" (register 33) thermostat will be set to 0. 
@soxs1987 can you confirm this?

@PimDoos Yes, I confirm this.
I think that you found the problem.

@PimDoos I am a newbie in home assistant. I think that I can change target_temp_register numbers in my PLC and I will fix the problem in a simple way.
If I want to make the correction in homeassistant/components/modbus/climate.py where can I find the file in my Home Assistant operating system? Thanks

The file you look for is in the modbus integration is in homeassistant/components/modbus/climate.py as you noted, but the location in your system  depends a lot on how you installed it (e.g. docker or manual install).

Remark if you want others to benefit from your change you need to make a PR and in order to do that you need to clone HA.

@janiversen I installed HA on a Raspberry Pi 3 with Home Assistant OS 5.12 (Hassio?). Can you tell me where is the file?
Another question, maybe offtopic. If I want to configure multiple modbus hosts (e.g. first name: hub1 type: tcp host: 192.168.123.49 second name: hub2 type: tcp host: 192.168.123.50) how can I configure climates? If I put hub:hub1 I get error and it doesn't work. Is it not possible? Thanks

@soxs1987 you need to look for it,I gave you the relative location.

you do not use hub/platform in climate since it is configured within the modbus. so if you have 2 modbus connections you have 2 climates. see doc https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/climate.modbus/
